overview: Cross-sectional study of all women referred to group pelvic floor classes in one year: booking records for everyone, a translated barrier survey, and linkage of answers to attendance for women who consent.
population: All 1,112 women referred between September 2025 and August 2026; excluded are women who died, moved away or asked not to be contacted, identified from the records before mailing.
exposure: Recorded: age, distance from home to hospital, interpreter need, referral source, parity where recorded. Reported: childcare, embarrassment in groups, class times, travel cost, symptom bother, preference for evening or online classes.
procedures: The administrator mails an information sheet, a 20-item questionnaire and a prepaid envelope, with a link and a telephone option in three languages; two reminders follow at two and four weeks. A consent box asks permission to link answers to the booking record. The physiotherapy lead extracts attendance and recorded factors for all referrals. Non-respondents are described from records only.

outcomes.name: Completion of four or more sessions
outcomes.measure: Four or more of six sessions attended, from the booking record
outcomes.why: The dose at which training is likely to help, and what the redesign aims to raise.

outcomes.name: Attendance at the first session
outcomes.measure: First session attended, from the booking record
outcomes.why: Separates never starting from dropping out.

outcomes.name: Survey response by attendance
outcomes.measure: Response proportion among attenders and non-attenders, by language
outcomes.why: Measures the main bias of the survey.

feasibility: About 1,100 mailings with two reminders fit the 1,500 budget; the administrator needs about three days; extraction of records takes the lead about four days.
biasMitigation: Records-based analysis for every referral, not only respondents
Two reminders and a telephone option to raise response among non-attenders
Translated materials and interpreter-supported telephone completion
Respondents compared with non-respondents on recorded factors, with inverse probability weights

biasFlags.label: Nonresponse among non-attenders
biasFlags.note: The central threat to the survey arm.

biasFlags.label: Recall of barriers
biasFlags.note: Some women were referred up to a year before the survey.

biasFlags.label: Inconsistent recording of interpreter need
biasFlags.note: Checked against language recorded at booking.

flags: Six pre-specified factors in the adjusted model
parsimony.simplestPath: One referral year, one records extract, one short survey, one primary outcome.

theoreticalFramework: None; the survey items come from the retrieved barrier studies and the service's own referral data.
summary: Linked records and survey study with one primary outcome and response bias measured.
